payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #350 (starting, resuming and rerunning a run admit through one runtime use case, before the dispatcher needs a fourth copy).

The branch story-350-launch-admission is on main 47b0d89b (after #429's #492 and #288 slice C's #493) and ends at 1ea74762, three commits. The story commit comes from implement-story-350-starting-res-6ad79353, which shipped after two returns (final chief: residual, low, no security residual). rebase-and-finish-story-350-star-e2209272 (residual, low) then rebased it onto #362 and #403, and made two changes. First, delivery.rs resolves --run through #362's selector::resolve_run before launch::resume and launch::rerun receive the id, so a LaunchRequest never carries a selector. Second, a follow-up commit, 17ec5e30, pins the exact line a missing run leaves under the selector. Exit codes come from #362's Exit enum. The controller's exact-coverage gate was green at 17ec5e30. The controller then rebased the branch onto 47b0d89b:
- setup.rs's imports are kept from both sides;
- #429's sweep report now sits in print_compiled, which compile and recipes show share, so both verbs print decision 0050's sweep on stderr alike;
- 1ea74762 makes show_and_compile_agree_for_every_recipe_under_every_realm_map read a compiled view by its stdout, because stderr now carries the sweep.
CI=true cargo test -p brokkr-cli passes all 44 suites. The controller's coverage gate runs again after this landing.

What it delivers:
- brokkr_runtime::launch::{start, resume, rerun}(LaunchRequest), returning an admitted Engine the CLI drives. A LaunchRequest is plain data (BundleSource, RunMap), so #430's dispatcher can build one without the CLI;
- every refusal at one site in launch, typed as LaunchError (decision 0071 ruling 8), with the operator's text unchanged. LaunchError::contention is the door the CLI asks, so a contended launch still exits 4;
- refuse_unboxable and its probe table moved from brokkr-cli/src/boundary.rs to brokkr-runtime/src/boundary.rs;
- one compile path (launch::compile_for) for run, rerun, compile, recipes show and doctor, so recipes show prints what compile prints under every map (tests/recipes.rs pins all 12 map and recipe pairs).

Two precedence changes the PR must ask the operator to rule on. Its Ruling line names both. They are not findings here unless the code differs from this description:
- the dispatch envelope is read, parsed and verified before the journal is opened. Beside a peer's lock on the journal, a bad envelope now exits 1 with its error, where the contention exited 4;
- when a realms map lies in the workspace, the ambient-map "not pinned" note is printed before a dispatch refusal, where the journal was opened first before.
Known lows, accepted as stated: resume compiles through compile_from_manifest in the pinned world and manifest realm (decision 0046 ruling 1), sharing compile_in_realm with compile_for. The envelope is verified in launch and again in Engine::start_with_dispatch, as that constructor's own guard.

Judge:
1. That every refusal keeps its text and exit code, and each entry point meets them in the order its CLI arm did, except the two precedence changes above. The rebase keeps #362's behaviour: every --run resolves through the selector, and verbs::tests::{resume,rerun}_resolves_latest and rerun_names_a_resolved_run_it_cannot_load pass unchanged. A missing --recipe never masks the refusal a verb met first (verbs::delivery::tests pins it per handler).
2. That no refusal was weakened or skipped on any entry point. The crossing fence, the unboxable host, realms-with-dispatch and the envelope bounds each refuse before a journal row is written, at start, rerun and resume alike.
3. That the public-API snapshot, the suppressions list and the guide (docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md) match the code. And that recipes show printing the 0050 sweep on stderr, like compile, is what the one compile path should do.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",

Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},

  ],

Read launch.rs and launch/tests.rs, runtime boundary.rs against the removed cli boundary.rs, verbs/delivery.rs old vs new plus delivery/tests.rs, setup.rs print_compiled/recipes show, doctor.rs, recipes.rs, lib.rs contention/report/Invocation/compile_in, engine.rs start_in_world/start_with_dispatch/resume and verify_dispatch_bundle_bounds, realms.rs World::load/discover/inspect/from_manifest, bundle.rs compile_with/compile_with_realm, and the recipes integration test.

The harness exports a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 pair, which breaks git; I unset it for git commands.

JUDGED, POSITIVE. (1) Text and exit codes are preserved: LaunchError variants flow through report to Exit::Failed(1), and Store/Engine contention through LaunchError::contention to Exit::Contended(4); LaunchError::SourceRun attaches its StoreError with #[source], so the CLI's chain-walking contention predicate still finds it. Each entry point meets refusals in the order its old CLI arm did (resume: journal->selector->manifest->recipe->compile->unboxable->engine->fence; rerun: map->journal->selector->load->feature->recipe->compile->unboxable->engine). The only inserted fence precedes recipe resolution for a world held from an earlier read, which the CLI already fenced in Invocation::resolve via World::load. (2) No refusal is weakened: named-map+dispatch, the crossing fence (admit_new for start/rerun, after Engine::resume for resume), refuse_unboxable, and verify_dispatch_bundle_bounds all fire before any journal row; read_dispatch verifies and the engine constructor re-checks. (3) The public-API snapshot, quality/suppressions.txt and docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md match the tree (ratchet api and the suppressions test pass); recipes show and compile share print_compiled, so both print the same stdout view and the same 0050 sweep on stderr.

The two operator-ruled precedence changes are present exactly as described and are not findings: read_dispatch (launch.rs:308-334) runs before Store::open, so a bad envelope beside a peer's lock now exits 1 with its text; and the ambient 'not pinned' note precedes that refusal.

CARRIED RESIDUAL LOWS (accepted as stated). (a) The dispatch envelope is verified and bounds-checked twice: in read_dispatch and again in Engine::start_with_dispatch (engine.rs:477-478), one rule written twice (ruling 5), kept as the constructor's own guard. (b) resume compiles through the private compile_from_manifest instead of the shared compile_for, sharing only the leaf compile_in_realm, so the one compile path holds for run/rerun/compile/recipes show/doctor but not resume (decision 0046 ruling 1).

No security residual: no fail-open path, no weakened or skipped refusal, no untyped vocabulary crossing a crate, and no error matched by its text was found.

result.notes:
Review chief on story-350-launch-admission, HEAD 1ea74762 over 47b0d89b, read-only: no file changed, nothing committed, tree clean.

PANEL. The joined result is residual (low, no security residual, no spec defect), reported by two positions named adversarial and correctness; this prompt speaks of correctness and security, and the adversarial notes answer the security questions (fail-open paths, weakened refusals, untyped vocabulary, text-matched errors). Neither position emitted anything addressed to the gate or arguing for a result; no member result was unreadable. The floor is residual and I rule residual at low; I confirmed each carried finding against the diff and add two of my own.

MY READ (judging points 1-3). (1) Text and exit codes hold. I diffed the old CLI arms (47b0d89b verbs/delivery.rs, lib.rs compile_in_realm/compile_from_manifest, boundary.rs) against launch.rs and the new handlers. Every operator line is byte-identical: RealmsWithDispatch, RecipeNotFound, the three Unboxable variants (seats: Vec<String> prints as the old Vec<&String> did), NoFeature, the bounds refusal via EngineError::Dispatch ('dispatch: dispatch execution bounds are unsafe'); ReadDispatch/ParseDispatch/SourceRun render through anyhow's {:#} chain exactly as the old .context lines did. Exit 4 flows through LaunchError::contention -> the CLI's contention() (delivery/tests pins Store, Engine::Store and a plain refusal); everything else exits 1. Order per entry point: run = Invocation::resolve (World::load fences) -> named+dispatch -> [fence again] -> recipe -> compile -> unboxable -> notice -> read -> parse -> verify -> bounds -> Store::open -> engine; rerun = resolve map -> open+selector (CLI) -> open -> load -> feature -> [fence] -> recipe -> compile -> unboxable -> engine; resume = open+selector (CLI) -> open -> manifest -> recipe -> compile_from_manifest -> unboxable -> Engine::resume -> fence. Each matches its old arm except the two ruled precedence changes, which are present exactly as the commission states (read_dispatch precedes Store::open; the ambient 'not pinned' note precedes the envelope refusal). #362 holds: every --run goes through selector::resolve_run in the handler before launch sees an id; verbs::tests::{resume,rerun}_resolves_latest and rerun_names_a_resolved_run_it_cannot_load are untouched by the diff and pass; delivery/tests pins that a missing --recipe never masks the refusal met first (RealmsWithDispatch line for run; 'no run matching' + Refusal::Missing for rerun and resume). (2) No refusal is weakened or skipped: named-map+dispatch, the crossing fence, refuse_unboxable and the envelope bounds each fire before any row at start, rerun and resume; launch/tests asserts the journal file is absent after each new-run refusal and the row counts unchanged after each rerun/resume refusal. Engine::start_with_dispatch keeps refuse_unbuilt, verify and bounds as its own guard; its refuse_unbuilt now sits after the launch's bounds check, which is unobservable because refuse_unboxable refuses the same unbuilt boundaries earlier on both the old and new paths. (3) quality/public-api/brokkr-runtime.txt grows by exactly the launch and boundary modules and every pub item has a consumer (ruling 6); quality/suppressions.txt is untouched and the new modules carry no suppression; docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md's sentence matches print_compiled. On the sweep: recipes show and compile share print_compiled, so both print the view on stdout and decision 0050's sweep on stderr; tests/recipes.rs asserts the (exit, stdout, stderr) triple equal for all 12 map/recipe pairs, so the sweep is pinned equal too. That is what one compile path should do: show is a compile of the recipe in the workspace's realm, and 0050 rules that a compile reports its checks without refusing. Agreed.

GATES. cargo test: brokkr-runtime launch:: (9 passed), brokkr-cli verbs::delivery + the three #362 selector tests + resume_compilation_reads_the_dialect (6 passed), tests/recipes.rs show_and_compile_agree_for_every_recipe_under_every_realm_map (passed, 1.7s). The panel ran fmt, clippy -D warnings, typos, ratchet files/clones/api and compile --bundle bundles/self clean; I did not repeat them and did not run coverage-exact.sh (the controller's).

SURVIVING FINDINGS, deduplicated (all low, none a return):
- [low, ruling 5; adversarial + correctness; named in the commission] The dispatch envelope is verified and bounds-checked in launch::read_dispatch and again in Engine::start_with_dispatch, one rule at two sites, kept as the constructor's own guard.
- [low, ruling 5 / decision 0046 ruling 1; adversarial + correctness; named in the commission] resume compiles through the private compile_from_manifest, not compile_for, sharing only compile_in_realm; its no-world branch is a separate Bundle::compile_with call.
